title: W08a: project registry and package foundation
description: Build the integration package skeleton and the single versioned project registry shared by the worker adapter and the Monitor: registrations with a generated stable key, a label, the canonical ledger root, the profile's explicit project-bound MCP server entry, a revision and an active or retired state. A Waystation project_id, a folder name or a remote URL is never the key, and duplicate filesystem aliases are detected. Registry configuration is local operational state outside the ledger, stored through the plugin's own profile-scoped state facility rather than a private file, with access scoped to the selected runtime and profile route and never a silent current-profile substitution. Settings may select a local root, but data endpoints accept only a registration key and record identifiers. Reassigning a root or server for a registration that bindings or calls reference is refused; retirement hides the project from ordinary selection and prohibits new bindings while preserving the pinned routing of existing bindings across restart, and hard deletion is refused while referenced. A genuinely missing or corrupt root errors explicitly and is never retargeted elsewhere.
acceptance: A registration key is stable across restarts and independent of folder name, project_id and remote URL, and duplicate filesystem aliases are detected on Windows junctions and case variants.
Worker and Monitor resolve registrations from the same store for the selected runtime and profile route, and browser storage never holds an authoritative project list.
Retirement preserves existing bindings across restart and blocks new ones, hard delete and root or server reassignment are refused while referenced, and a missing root errors without retargeting.
Configuration writes are atomic under a short plugin-config lock that is never held while waiting on a ledger lock or an MCP request.
notes: Acceptance group A14. The integration lives at integrations/hermes/ in this repository with generic ledger behavior staying in src/core/. Adding or changing project MCP entries changes the tool surface and invalidates the provider prompt cache, so registration churn is a rollout-policy decision.
